If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3–5 days, reduce forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3–5 days, increase forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to counteract pessimism.

If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative within 3 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% in mid-horizon (8–15 days) to reflect sentiment reversal risk.

If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast in late horizon (16–30 days) to capture momentum continuation.

If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast in late horizon (16–30 days) to avoid overcorrection.

If sentiment is mixed (alternating 0.33–0.67) and forecast deviates >1.5% from recent history, apply a 0.5–1.0% correction in mid-horizon to smooth out erratic sentiment-driven noise.
